source: gh issue view <N> --json state,closedAt  — one call per issue, RE-READ at 2026-11-02T14:22:24Z (all five states a row depends on: 5333 OPEN, 9736 OPEN, 10360 OPEN, 9596 OPEN, 5087 OPEN; the six CLOSED states re-confirmed unchanged)
why: V12 of tools/capstone_verdict_check.py: a row's `blocked_by` is a provenance POINTER, and a pointer at CLOSED work is stale evidence by construction. Until #10537 the checker verified only the pointer's FORM (`#NNN`), so three of the five rows of the shipped table named issues that had already closed while the gate printed `structurally sound` (E2<-9775 two days late, E4<-8503 nine days, E5<-9738 that morning). The states live in this committed record rather than a network call so the check stays pure, offline and deterministic in CI; a lane refreshes it from the tracker when it re-measures and commits it WITH the measurement it verifies, so the state that decides a row is reviewed in the same diff as the row.
refresh: For each issue a row cites: `gh issue view <N> --json state,closedAt`, then update checked_at. A record that is present but malformed is a usage error (exit 2), never a silent disarm.
